{{nihongo|'''Hotaka Shrine'''|穂高神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

In addition to the main shrine (satomiya) in Hotaka, Azumino City, there is also Myojin Pond in {{ill|Kamikōchi|Q1048234|qid=Q1048234}} in {{ill|Matsumoto, Nagano|Q213324|qid=Q213324}} in Azumino. (Matsumoto City)|Q11512587|Okunomiya}}, {{ill|Mount Hotakadake|Q656026|qid=Q656026|lt=Mt. Okuhotaka}} Because there is a shrine at the top of Mt., it is commonly known as ``the total guardian of the {{ill|Japanese Alps|Q645773|qid=Q645773}}.'' Also, the annual festival (Mifune Festival) held every year on {{ill|September 27|Q2884|qid=Q2884}} is famous.

=== Enshrined God ===
The deities enshrined at the main shrine are as follows. The main enshrined deity is in bold.
* Chudono: '''{{ill|Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|Q86736058|qid=Q86736058|lt=Hotakami-no-Mikoto}}''' (Hotakami no Mikoto) - Another name is "Utsushi Nikin Kin-no-Mikoto." Child of Watatsumi no Mikoto.
* Sadono: '''{{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi no Mikoto}}''' (Watatsumi no Mikoto) - The god of the sea and the ancestor of the Azumi clan.

=== About the enshrined deity ===
Since ancient times, the area around Hotaka Shrine has been known as the settlement area of the {{ill|Azumi people|Q3377806|qid=Q3377806|lt=Azumi}} (accurately speaking, currently only the Azumi clan has been confirmed) and the Azumi Inukai clan <ref name="Hotaka history"/>, and can also be seen as the name of Azumi {{ill|Gunji|Q4152149|qid=Q4152149}} in the Nara period. There is {{ill|Azumi Basin|Q4833082|qid=Q4833082}} as a place name around the shrine. The following three articles are known to be related to the Azumi clan in "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}}" <ref name="Hotaka History">"History and Landscape Hotaka Shrine" pp. 2-3. </ref>.
* Ukyojinbetsu Azumi Sukunejo - After Hodakami no Mikoto, the son of {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=sea god Watatsumi Toyotamahikokami}}.
* Ukyojinbetsu Bonkairenjo - After Hodakami no Mikoto, the son of Kaijin Watazumi no Mikoto.
* Kawachi no Kuni Kamibetsu Azumi Renjo - After the son of the sea god Watazumi no Mikoto, Hotakami no Mikoto.The Hodaka clan, {{ill|Shake (social class)|Q11588367|qid=Q11588367}} of Hotaka Shrine, is a descendant of Hotakami no Mikoto, and the theory that the deity enshrined at Hotaka Shrine is ``Hotakami no Mikoto'' is based on the relationship between the company name, these historical materials, and the history of the shrine and its surroundings. Furthermore, in the Jindaiki "{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}", there is a mention of "{{ill|Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|Q86736058|qid=Q86736058}}" as the son of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watatsumi-sanjin}} (Watatsumi-kami and Watazumi-kami) and the founder of the Azumi clan, but another name for this god is said to be Hotakamino-Mikoto.<ref name="Hotaka history"/>. Other children of Watatsumi no Mikoto include {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyotama Bime no Mikoto}}, the wife of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hikohihodemi no Mikoto}}, and {{jalink|Tamayoribime, the wife of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ubuki Kusabuki Fugyou no Mikoto}} and the mother of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}}. (Hyuga mythology)|Q3082751|Tamayibime no Mikoto}} exists.

On the other hand, there is a theory that the company name ``Hotaka Shrine'' simply means ``the shrine of the gods of Hotaka'' or ``the shrine that sits in Hotaka'' <ref name="Gods"/>.

In addition, in ancient times, the enshrined deity was one troupe (in the Engishiki Shinmyocho), but in the Middle Ages there were three shrines: Omiya, Minamigu, and Wakamiya, and in a document dated 18 ({{ill|1549|Q6554|qid=Q6554}}), Gosho Daimyojin (deity unknown) was also referred to as Gosho (deity unknown).<ref name="Place name">Hotaka Shrine section of "Place name of Nagano prefecture". </ref>.

Founding date is unknown. The enshrined area is in the {{ill|Azumi district|ja|安曇郡|qid=Q11450769}} district, and it is thought to have been established by the established {{ill|Azumi people|Q3377806|qid=Q3377806|lt=Azumbe clan}}, and it is said that the ancestral god was enshrined by the Azumbe clan.<ref name="Gods"/>

There are various theories about how the Azumi clan settled in Azumi District (for details, see "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Azumi clan#Distribution of the Azumi clan}}"). There is also {{ill|Kawaai Shrine|ja|川会神社|qid=Q85879982}} in {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} in Azumi District, but here too {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watatsumijin}} of the Azumi clan is said to be the enshrined deity <ref name="Gods"/>. Many ancient tombs were built to the west of Hotaka Shrine, but the area around Hotaka Shrine is thought to have been avoided as a sacred area, and the area around Hotaka Shrine is thought to have been the center of power.The first sight of the Azumi clan in Azumi District is an ink calligraphy dated {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|de|Tempyō-Hōji|es|Tenpyō-hōji|fa|تنپیو-هوجی|fr|Ère Tenpyō-hōji|ia|Tenpyo-hoji|id|Tempyō-hōji|ja|天平宝字|ko|덴표호지|ru|Тэмпё-ходзи|simple|Tenpyō-hōji|sr|Тенпјо хоџи|tr|Tenpyō-hōji|uk|Темпьо-Ходзі (ненґо)|zh|天平宝字|zh_yue|天平寶字|qid=Q1346307}}8 ({{ill|764|Q31163|qid=Q31163}}) found on a {{ill|Shōsōin|Q2379007|qid=Q2379007}} treasured cloth hakama.<ref name="Gods"/> However, since there is only a mention of ``Azumi-bu'' here, there is a theory that Mr. Azumi's {{ill|bu-kyoku|Q5046108|qid=Q5046108}} was simply installed in this area. </ref>.

=== Outline ===
The first appearance of the document is that on February 11, {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} 3rd year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), ``Hotakujin'' was promoted {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.<ref name="Gods">``Japanese Gods'' Hotaka Shrine section. </ref>. In "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, "Hotaka Shrine It is listed as ``Meishin Taisha'' and is listed as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}. Also, as seen in the ``Sannomiya Hotakasha Gozogu Jo Nikki'' written in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 13 ({{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}}), Sannomiya of Shinano Province was called <ref> ``Japanese Medieval States and the Ichinomiya System of the Provinces'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 55. </ref>.When the {{ill|Nishina clan|Q11376452|qid=Q11376452}}, the local feudal lord who had ruled the Azumi district since the Middle Ages, fell, Azumi district became the territory of the {{ill|Matsumoto Castle|Q739612|qid=Q739612|lt=Lord of Matsumoto Castle}}, and in 10 years ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} {{ill|Ogasawara Sadayoshi|Q10856562|qid=Q10856562}}, who became the lord of the castle in 1582|Q6719}}, donated the land as a divine territory, and from {{ill|Ogasawara Hidemasa|Q8192119|qid=Q8192119}} passed it down from generation to generation, striving to carry out shrine transfers and rituals in ceremonial years.<ref name="Hotaka history"/>.

In ancient times, it was influenced by Suwa Taisha Shrine, and according to the "Jijiki" there was a south shrine in the precincts that enshrined the Suwa god, and there was also a custom of erecting pillars. It was also strongly influenced by Buddhism, and according to documents, there was a Jingu-ji temple within the precincts in the Middle Ages, and in the Edo period, there was a Yakushi-do hall to the southwest of the main hall, which served as the main hall <ref name="place name"/>. During the {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} years ({{ill|1592|Q6769|qid=Q6769}} - {{ill|1596|ab|1596|af|1596|als|1596|am|1596 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1596|ar|1596|ary|1596|arz|1596|ast|1596|avk|1596|az|1596|azb|۱۵۹۶ (میلادی)|bar|1596|bcl|1596|be|1596|be_x_old|1596|bg|1596|bn|১৫৯৬|bpy|মারি ১৫৯৬|br|1596|bs|1596.|ca|1596|cdo|1596 nièng|ce|1596 шо|ceb|1596|ckb|١٥٩٦|crh|1596|cs|1596|cv|1596|cy|1596|da|1596|de|1596|diq|1596|el|1596|eml|1596|eo|1596|es|1596|et|1596|eu|1596|fa|۱۵۹۶ (میلادی)|fi|1596|fo|1596|fr|1596|frr|1596|fur|1596|fy|1596|ga|1596|gan|1596年|gcr|1596|gd|1596|gl|1596|gv|1596|he|1596|hi|१५९६|hif|1596|hr|1596.|ht|1596 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1596|hy|1596|hyw|1596 թուական|ia|1596|id|1596|ilo|1596|io|1596|is|1596|it|1596|ja|1596年|jv|1596|ka|1596|kaa|1596|kk|1596 жыл|ko|1596년|krc|1596 джыл|la|1596|lb|1596|lij|1596|lmo|1596|lt|1596 m.|lv|1596. gads|mai|१५९६|map_bms|1596|mdf|1596|mg|1596|mhr|1596|mi|1596|mk|1596|mr|इ.स. १५९६|mrj|1596 и|ms|1596|my|၁၅၉၆|mzn|۱۵۹۶|nah|1596|nap|1596|nds|1596|new|सन् १५९६|nl|1596|nn|1596|no|1596|nrm|1596|nso|1596|oc|1596|olo|1596|or|୧୫୯୬|os|1596-æм аз|pl|1596|pnb|1596|pt|1596|qu|1596|ro|1596|ru|1596 год|rue|1596|sa|१५९६|sah|1596 сыл|sc|1596|scn|1596|sd|1596ع|se|1596|sh|1596.|shn|1596|simple|1596|sk|1596|sl|1596|smn|1596|sq|1596|sr|1596|su|1596|sv|1596|sw|1596|ta|1596|tg|Соли 1596|th|พ.ศ. 2139|tk|1596|tl|1596|tly|1596|tr|1596|tt|1596 ел|uk|1596|ur|1596ء|uz|1596|vec|1596|vi|1596|vls|1596|wa|1596|war|1596|wuu|1596年|xmf|1596|yi|1596|zea|1596|zh|1596年|zh_min_nan|1596 nî|zh_yue|1596年|qid=Q6785}}), 15 koku of red seals were enshrined at Hotaka Shrine and 3 koku of red seals were enshrined at Jingu-ji Temple <ref name="place name"/>.

=== Precincts ===

=== Motomiya (Satomiya) ===
[[File:Hotaka-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|main hall}}{{Small|The style of the middle hall is called ``Hotaka-zukuri''. }}]]
The main shrine has a three-dono structure, with the right shrine, middle shrine, and left shrine all having the same format, and these three shrines are lined up with the smaller Shinmeisha Shrine. Among these, the central shrine has a unique form of ``Chigi'' and ``Katsuogi'' that are passed down only to Hotaka Shrine. Katsuogi is said to represent a fishing rod or a ship's mast, and this form is called ``Hotaka-zukuri.''<ref>History and Landscape Hotaka Shrine, p. 4. </ref>. At the Sengu Festival held in Shikinen, the shrine buildings are remodeled and rearranged according to the method specified in the ``Jijiki.''

In the precincts, the Kagura Hall stands in front of the worship hall, and to the right of it are Wakamiya Shrine and several shrine shrines. In addition, the hand-washing stone, the chozuya, and the Shinbashi bridge are designated cultural properties by Azumino City, and the Daimon zelkova and Wakamiya Nishi zelkova are designated natural monuments by Azumino City.

Hotaka Shrine is listed in the ``Zenkoji Domeisho Zue'' of 14 years ({{ill|1843|Q7629|qid=Q7629}}), which gives us an idea of ​​what the precincts looked like at that time.

=== Okumiya ===
[[File:150920 Hotaka-jinja Okumiya Kamikochi Japan03n.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Okumiya Haisho}}]]
Okumiya is located in Kamikochi, Azumi, Matsumoto City. It rests at the entrance of {{ill|Myōjin Pond|ja|明神池 (松本市)|qid=Q11512587|lt=Myojin Pond}} in {{ill|Chūbu-Sangaku National Park|Q764357|qid=Q764357}}. Myojin Pond, a scenic spot next to Okumiya, is within the grounds of the same shrine and is {{ill|shin'iki|Q11588853|qid=Q11588853}}. The enshrined deity is Hotakami no Kami, and the main shrine is built in Hotakazukuri.

Unlike the main shrine, the Mifune ritual at Okumiya is held on October 8th every year by floating a boat on Myojin Pond. Additionally, the opening festival will be held on April 27th and the closing festival will be held on November 15th.

The name ``Kamikochi'' (Kamikochi, Kamigaki) is said to have come from the fact that the Hotaka Shrine Okumiya, which enshrines the deity Hotakami, and Myojin Pond are located here.

=== Minemiya ===
Minegu Shrine is enshrined at the top of Mt. Okuhotakadake (3,190{{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}}), where the god Hotakami is said to have descended ({{Coord|36|1 7|21.14|N|137|38|52.81|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|name=Reimiya (top of Mt. Okuhotakadake)}}). The shrine building is a small shrine made of white stone.

=== Festival ===

=== Shikinen Festival ===
As part of the Shikinen Festival, the ``Daisaku Sengu Festival'' is held once every 20 years, in which the entire main shrine building is rebuilt, and the ``Small Sengu Festival'', in which repairs are carried out twice during that period. The festival is held in an old style that dates back to before 1483, according to the ``Sannomiya Hotaka Shrine Gozogu Jo Nikki'' (a cultural property designated by Azumino City) handed down at Hotaka Shrine, and has been designated as an intangible folk cultural property by Azumino City.

The Shinto ritual begins with the Shishisakakitate Shinto ritual 100 days before the transfer. Once the main shrines had finished their functions, they were given away to each company or demolished, and then relocated, and only about a dozen buildings still exist today.

=== Annual festival ===
* Saidansai, long live Seiju, prayers for the safety of parishioners and worshipers (January 1st)
* Grand Peace and Traffic Safety Prayer Festival (January 1st - 8th)
* Special prayer festival for warding off evil spirits and warding off evil spirits (January Coming of Age Day)
* Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Prayer Festival, Hosha Festival (special ritual), prayer for the promotion of agriculture, industry, commerce, and industry (March 17th)
* Kangakusai (last Sunday in March)
* War Memorial Festival (Peace Prayer Festival) (April 20th)
* Great Purification Ceremony (Prayer to ward off misfortune) (June 30th)
* Ancestry Festival (August 2nd)
* Hongu Reitaisai (September 26th - 27th)
** Yoimiya (September 26th)
** Main festival (September 27) - Mifune Shinto ritual (designated intangible folk cultural property by Nagano Prefecture).
* Okumiya Festival (October 8th)
* Shinjosai, Reikaku Anniversary Festival (November 19th)
* Great Purification Ceremony, New Year's Eve Festival (December 31st)

=== Mifune Festival ===
[[File:Hotaka-jinja ofune.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mifune}}]]
The annual festival is called ``''Mifune Festival'' and is held on September 26th and 27th every year. It is a heroic festival where large boat-shaped {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} (dashi) ``Ofune'' (dashi), which are 6 meters high and 12 meters long, are collided with each other, and has been designated as an intangible folk cultural property by Nagano Prefecture. The 26th is only a Shinto ritual, and the main festival is on the 27th. September 27th is said to be the death anniversary of Hirafu Azumi, who was killed in the {{ill|Battle of Baekgang|Q608727|qid=Q608727}} in the second year of Emperor Tenji ({{ill|663|Q31122|qid=Q31122}}).

During the festival, five large and small boats are decorated with Hotaka dolls and {{ill|Ujiko|ja|氏子|qid=Q125562175}} parade the boats through the streets of Hotaka and the countryside. They are then towed to the shrine, paraded around the Kagura hall within the shrine grounds, and as they are towed around the shrine, the two large ships violently collide with each other. It attracts many visitors due to its power and splendor. There is also a ``Children's Festival'' held on the first Saturday and Sunday of September, where children's boats are paraded through the town.

The Mifune used in the Mifune ritual is on display at the Mifune Kaikan (admission fee: 300 yen for adults) on the north side of the main shrine. The structure of the Mifune consists of a turret (elongated cube), four wheels, a mountain (hanging tree, mawashiki, and trestle tree), and a belly (the front is a man's belly, and the rear is a woman's belly). During Shinto rituals, young people sit inside the boat and play instruments such as flutes and drums.

=== Hosha Festival ===
``Obishasai'' is a special Shinto ritual held on March 17th. From the center of the worship hall, shoot the ``God's Arrow'' to the northeast and the ``Dono's Arrow'' to the southeast, then shoot the 12 feather arrows lowered into the Kagura Hall. It is said that the way the arrow hits the target predicts whether the year will be good or bad.<ref>History and Landscape of Hotaka Shrine, p. 12. </ref>. The ritual is designated as an intangible folk cultural property by Azumino City.

=== Mifune Kaikan ===
Opened in 1982. It was established as a place to permanently introduce the Mifune and Gofurei rituals that characterize Hotaka Shrine, the Mifune collision, and the traditional Hotaka dolls, as well as explain the history of the Hotaka Shrine Sengu ritual and the rebuilding of the main shrine, as well as the Hotaka Shrine Okumiya and Minemiya <ref name=A>[https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/museum/jinja/16/16_hotaka.html Hotaka Shrine and Museum (Mifune Kaikan)] Kokugakuin University Graduate School</ref>.

The building area is 760 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}, the building structure is a two-story steel frame structure, and the collection is approximately 250 items. The main items in the collection include Mifune, Hotaka dolls, ancient documents (``Shinano Province Sannomiya Hotaka Shrine construction diary''), Dosojin, votive tablets, furniture, costumes, Hotaka doll decorations (historical picture scrolls), etc. <ref name=A/>.
